subject: FinCo production: sudden p95/p99 regression — cold-starts on hosted GPU pools
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen.li@finco.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: api-platform@finco.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Marcus —

We started seeing a sharp regression in p95 and p99 latency for token-generation calls to your Hosted API at ~14:50 PST. Error rates for ModelX-3b increased from ~0.3% to 2.8% and p99 went from ~420ms to ~2.1s. This is affecting our real-time payment auth path.

Attached are a short span sample and SLO window. We see the pattern on both eu-west and us-west regions (but worse in us-west). Can you confirm whether autoscale or cold-start behavior changed today? We had no config changes on our side.

This is high-severity for us — our on-call is paged. Please advise immediate mitigation and when we can expect a fix.

Thanks,
Karen
SRE Lead, FinCo

Attachments: p95-spike-traces-20261120.log, span-sample-20261120.jsonl

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@finco.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Karen — thank you for the flags and the logs. We see the traces in your attachment. I’ve opened SUP-4321 and looped in engineering and the incident lead.

Immediate items:
- We will enable a temporary warm-pool for your Dedicated routing (5 GPUs) within the hour to eliminate cold-start tail for your traffic.
- We will put a rule to route your traffic to our lowest-latency pool while we investigate root cause.
- We’ll share a timeline and a postmortem.

Jonas — can you post an initial assessment of whether the spike correlates with a kernel module or container startup regression?

Karen — I’ll send a short maintenance plan and ETA in the next 30 minutes.

—Marcus
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Quick initial read from the traces: several p99s originate from requests that landed on freshly provisioned GPU instances where model weights were still being loaded into device memory (cold-start). We’re seeing long NVCache population times (700ms-1.5s) when the sequence-length distribution spikes. There are also a small set of failed requests matched to OOM-retries that surfaced as transient 5xx.

Hypothesis: a change in our autoscaler’s spin-up behavior (priority of kernel warmup vs. accept-connections) allowed ingress to hit instances before weight cache was ready. I’ll validate with infra logs (kernel startup, container init) and provide the earliest commit/time that changed autoscale gating.

Mitigations we can apply immediately:
- Hold new-connections until KV cache ready flag is reported (fast patch).
- Pre-warm a minimal pool for FinCo (config toggle) — Marcus’ mitigation.
- Temporarily lower the autoscale aggressiveness to force warm instances to be kept alive for 5 extra minutes.

I’ll push logs to SUP-4321 and post an ETA in 20m.

—Jonas
SRE, Inference Runtime

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karen Li <karen.li@finco.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Karen — I’ve applied a routing rule to move FinCo traffic to our warm-optimized pool and requested a warm-pool scale-up (5x small GPUs) as Marcus noted. You should see p95/p99 improve within the next 15–25 minutes; I’ll monitor and report back.

For transparency, we will also provision a short-term credit for the incident window (TBD by finance) and open a formal RCA.

I’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes until the SLO returns to normal.

—Stephanie
Director, Customer Operations

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Karen Li <karen.li@finco.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:19:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Follow-up: infra confirms a regression introduced in an autoscaler commit earlier today that changed the readiness gating order. The brief timeline:
- 14:05 PST: autoscaler rollout (commit a3f9d1) pushed to hosted pools to optimize spin-up latency.
- 14:47 PST: first FinCo p99 spike observed.

The fix is a rollback of the gating change and an additional readiness probe that ensures KV cache population completes before accepting traffic. I’m kicking a rollback now and starting a canary for the probe patch.

Expected user-visible improvement after rollback: p99 should retreat toward baseline within ~10 minutes after the rollback finishes and warm-pool routing is in place.

Logs and traces are attached to SUP-4321 and console link.

—Jonas

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@finco.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: API errors / latency spike - urgent

Karen — final update for the incident window:

Timeline summary:
- 14:05 PST: autoscaler change deployed (we made a change intended to reduce spin-up latency but it altered readiness ordering).
- 14:47 PST: FinCo p95/p99 spike reported by you.
- 15:12 PST: warm-pool routing applied; temporary warm pool provisioned by ops.
- 15:24 PST: rollback of gating change completed; canary for the readiness probe in place.
- 15:35 PST: metrics show p99 returning toward baseline; error rate back to ~0.35%.

Next steps:
- Jonas will open a postmortem and propose a permanent readiness probe and a pre-warm tier for high-impact customers (SUP-4321).
- We will offer FinCo a credit for the incident window and include an SLA amendment for pre-warm options for critical paths.
- Engineering will add a GA feature to prevent accepting traffic until KV cache reports ready on new instances.

Appreciate your patience — we’ll follow up with the full RCA and remediation plan in SUP-4321 and HubSpot HS-44219. If you want a synchronous postmortem sync, we can set that up next week.

—Marcus
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
